spendNote: Nothing was generated. The check read a film that already existed on staging, out of the object store, and wrote nothing back.

film.what: the titled cut of the first ElevenLabs-voiced film, recorded in docs/evidence/release-2/elevenlabs-voiced.json

findings.message: The picture is black for 8–8.87 s, 12.47–13.97 s. Confirm this is the cut and not a missing render.
The picture does not change for 4–6 s, 6–8 s. Confirm this is a held frame and not a stalled render.
Luma reaches 11–253, outside the 16–235 this delivery's limited range allows. Levels will be clipped by a conforming player.

corroboration.note: That record's output block was measured by hand with ffmpeg and typed into the file. Every number the check produces for the same film matches it: 14.0 s, h264, aac, 48000 Hz, 2 channels, 548271 bytes, -29.7 dB mean and -3.4 dB max. The hand measurement was right; it simply had no code behind it.

findingsRead.reading: Expected, and worth seeing stated. 0.87 s of black sits between the film and the credits, and the last 1.5 s of the credits card is black. That is 2.4 s of a 14 s film with nothing on screen.
findingsRead.action: none — the Editor's titled cut is what it is. A creator should be told, which is what the finding does.

findingsRead.reading: Expected on this run: the picture pool was mock, and a mock shot is a held frame. On a live render this finding would mean something quite different.
findingsRead.action: none. It is the check working, not a defect.

findingsRead.reading: The real finding. The delivered master carries luma from 11 to 253, outside the 16-235 its limited-range H.264 signalling promises, so a conforming player will clip both ends. Nothing in the picture path converts range: the graphics are generated as full-range RGBA and the conform encodes yuv420p without an explicit range conversion.
findingsRead.action: an operator decision, recorded as a known gap rather than fixed here. The fix is a range conversion in the render path, which is a deterministic filter change and must be specified to the bit-exact standard the picture recipes hold.

knownGaps: Nothing calls this check in the product yet. It was run here by hand against a delivered master; where it runs, who sees it and whether a review verdict blocks anything is a later increment.
The illegal luma range is not fixed. It is a render-path change, and a grade or range conversion has to meet the same bit-exact standard as every other filter stage in the conform.
One film, on one host, with the picture pool on mock. This is the first check, not a corpus.
Safe area, caption overflow, decodability across players, colour accuracy and HDR were not checked, as the report itself says.
